s.g: (countable, informal) A café.
(countable, informal) A cafeteria.
(countable, uncountable) A caffeinated coffee.
(South Africa) A convenience store, originally one that sold coffee and similar basic items.

cafe.f: (automotive) Acronym of Corporate Average Fuel Economy.

s.g: (chiefly Latino) A small hot coffee drink, particularly Cuban espresso.
(chiefly US, Canada) A restaurant in which customers select their food at a counter then carry it on a tray to a table to eat.
(chiefly US, Canada) A dining area in an institution where meals may be purchased (as above), provided, or brought in from elsewhere.
A cylindrical glass or metal jug, fitted with a filter on a rod, used to make coffee.
(UK, Ireland, slang) Synonym of café.
of, or pertaining to coffee or caffeic acid
(transitive) To add caffeine to something.
(intransitive, slang) To drink caffeinated beverages in order to increase one's energy or wakefulness or to enhance physical or mental performance.
(transitive, slang) To inject tension into (a situation, etc.) for one's own amusement; to stir things up.
(transitive, slang) To provoke (a person) for one's own amusement.
Containing caffeine naturally (e.g., coffee, tea, and cacao) or as an additive (e.g., soft drinks, sports drinks, or energy drinks).
(informal, of a person) Overly peppy or energetic; stimulated by caffeine.

caffeinated.f: simple past and past participle of caffeinate

s.g: An alkaloid, C₈H₁₀N₄O₂, found naturally in tea and coffee plants, which acts as a mild stimulant on the central nervous system.
A velvet material popularly used in upholstery.
An Italian café.

cafo.f: (agriculture) Initialism of concentrated animal feeding operation.

cafs.f: Initialism of compressed air foam system.

s.g: A coffee shop; an establishment selling coffee and sometimes other non-alcoholic beverages, simple meals or snacks, with a facility to consume them on the premises.
(Canada) A small restaurant of any genre.
